correctness.rationale: After setting z=x-y, the problem is to classify x,z,x-z on the octagonal unit sphere. Dihedral symmetry moves x to the vertical edge x=(1,a). Direct edge intersections produce exactly three parameter branches, plus the exchange z<->x-z. On the outer branches one midline length is identically c=2sqrt2-1 and the other is monotone up to c; on the middle branch the exact formulas are (2+r-a)/sqrt2 and (2+r+a)/sqrt2 with |a|<=r^2, so both are <=c. At a=-r the explicit pair attains both bounds. Coordinatewise monotonicity of the three defining objectives then gives the stated M1, M2, M3 values.
risks: The edge-classification argument depends on the stated regular-octagon normalization; affine-equivalent normalizations require coordinate conversion.
The finite checker confirms sampled intersections but the exhaustive continuum proof is the analytic branch derivation.

value.rationale: The result is not merely three isolated numerical evaluations. It determines a sharp coordinatewise envelope for the two midline lengths on every equilateral unit triangle in a canonical non-Hilbert regular polygon. That stronger statement immediately resolves the arithmetic, quadratic and subduplicate constants and explains why distinct mean objectives share one common maximizer. It also sharpens comparison with the known geometric-mean invariant on exactly the same admissible set.
risks: The theorem is a canonical exact polygonal benchmark rather than a classification of all polygonal Banach planes.
